findings.area: DI lifetime vs runtime configuration replacement
findings.description: IArtworkImageAccess and IArtworkSourceReader are registered with TryAddSingleton and their factories capture ConfigurationSnapshotService.Current.Limits once at first resolution. A runtime TryReplace of the configuration would leave both services enforcing stale byte/dimension limits. The outcome stays safe either way (a stale larger limit is still re-checked by the renderer against the current RenderRequest limits, and a stale smaller limit fails conservatively), and the same pattern already exists for StateRepository from task 5.2, so this is not blocking.
findings.recommended_action: If runtime configuration replacement is enabled before publication (5.5), either re-read Current.Limits per read or document that limits changes require a plugin reload.

findings.area: ActiveImageIdentity dimension semantics vs data model
findings.description: The adapter records post-orientation display dimensions in ActiveImageIdentity.Width/Height, while docs/data-model.md 3.10.1 describes width/height as 'Supporting Jellyfin image metadata'. This is self-consistent because every recorded and fresh observation is produced by the same adapter, and PNG-derived active images have no orientation offset, so no ownership false-positive/negative results. The worker disclosed this. The data-model wording could be reconciled later.
findings.recommended_action: In a later documentation pass, state that the adapter records oriented display dimensions as the supporting width/height identity values.

findings.description: The worker summary states the only added production MediaBrowser.* references are in JellyfinArtworkImageAccess.cs. The composition root ArrTagsServiceRegistrator also adds using MediaBrowser.Controller.Drawing and MediaBrowser.Controller.Library so it can resolve ILibraryManager and IImageProcessor for the factory. This is normal DI wiring, not entity/access leakage, and the renderer and the adapter result remain Jellyfin-free.
findings.recommended_action: None required; the composition-root references are necessary and do not violate the boundary.

findings.description: The PNG/JPEG confinement is enforced in the host adapter (and re-checked in the reader), not inside the renderer. SourceImageInput still accepts any content type beginning with 'image/', so a future caller that bypasses IArtworkSourceReader could re-introduce the Phase 4 gap. This matches the finding's recommended action (which explicitly targets the host source adapter) and the task instruction not to modify the renderer, so the assigned finding is genuinely closed for the supported path.
findings.recommended_action: Keep all production source capture on IArtworkSourceReader; do not add other SourceImageInput producers.

findings.description: For an item whose active image is not local, JellyfinArtworkImageAccess calls ILibraryManager.ConvertImageToLocal, which downloads the image, persists it through ProviderManager.SaveImage, and updates the item repository during a source read. This mirrors the pinned ImageController.GetImageInternal read path and uses removeOnFailure:false, and the worker disclosed it, but it is a host-side mutation performed before publication (5.5) exists.
findings.recommended_action: Later publication/lifecycle tasks (5.5/5.8/5.9) should account for the fact that capturing a remote source materializes it locally and updates the item.

findings.description: ArtworkSourceContentType.TryDetect duplicates the PNG/JPEG magic-byte logic already present in SourceArtifactFormat.DetectContentType. The duplication is intentional: the artifact store accepts a wider container set for storage while the source adapter must confine to the two renderer-inspected containers. No correctness issue.
findings.recommended_action: Optional future refactor to share the primitive signature check while keeping ArtworkSourceContentType.IsConfined as the gate.

summary: Task 5.3 is independently APPROVED. The adapter is well-scoped and correctly separates the Jellyfin-free host-neutral core (IArtworkSourceReader/ArtworkSourceReader, SourceImageDescriptor) from the single MediaBrowser.* implementation (JellyfinArtworkImageAccess), with the injectable IArtworkImageAccess seam. It reads the unindexed Primary (index 0) surface, maps Present/Absent/Failed to a bounded result, enforces the OperationalLimits source byte and decoded-dimension bounds, detects the container from magic bytes (not extension), computes SHA-256/byte length, derives post-orientation display dimensions with the exact renderer mapping, and can build both a valid SourceImageInput and the task 5.2 ActiveImageIdentity from one bounded read with no path/entity/DTO/credential leakage. Content-type confinement to PNG/JPEG signatures genuinely closes the carried-forward Phase 4 MEDIUM finding for the supported source path without touching the renderer. DI registration is lazy (no startup work) and the lifetime is singleton; the only caveat is captured limits that would go stale on a runtime configuration replacement (safe and consistent with the existing StateRepository pattern). Build is clean (0 warnings/0 errors) and all counts were reproduced: default 740/49/789, forced-native 813/6/819, focused 61/4/65 default and 72/0/72 forced. Guard honesty was independently confirmed: the native-guarded cases fail (not silently pass) when ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT=1 is set without the pinned native runtime. Scope is correct: no packaging (5.4), publication/SaveImage (5.5), ArtworkOperation journal (5.6), reconciliation (5.7), pipeline preservation (5.8), lifecycle fencing (5.9), Enhanced coexistence (5.10), route/client tests (5.11), RenderVersion change, ADR change, or lock-file change is present. Docs (PLANS, README, architecture, changelog, readiness, research) are accurate. No blockers or required changes.
